title: Prime-to-ell residue degree after arbitrary field extension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $L/k$ a finite field extension of degree $d$ [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $\ell$ be a prime with $\ell\nmid d$, and let $K/k$ be any field extension. Form the scheme
$$P=\operatorname{Spec}L\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$$
[def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. Every point $z$ of $P$ has $[\kappa(z):K]$ finite, and at least one such point has $\ell\nmid[\kappa(z):K]$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The residue fields are those of $L\otimes_k K$, where the tensor algebra has multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$. No separability or finiteness assumption is imposed on $K/k$.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 1.2.7, printed pp. 25--26: its field-theoretic assertion, with arbitrary extension K/k; separate the separable and purely inseparable parts.

proof.text: Put $A=L\otimes_k K$, viewed as a $K$-algebra through $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. The affine fibre-product theorem [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $P$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$, compatibly with its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Each of $\operatorname{Spec}L$, $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has one point with residue field the indicated field [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] gives a bijection between points $z$ of $P$ and prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of $A$. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] identifies $\kappa(z)$ with the fraction field of $A/\mathfrak p$, as an extension of $K$. In particular, whenever $A/\mathfrak p$ is a field, it is precisely $\kappa(z)$ as a $K$-field.

source.place: Tags 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes) and 01JT (lemma-points-fibre-product), including the residue-field sentence

proof.text: Choose a $k$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $L$ and its coordinate maps $\lambda_i:L\to k$. The tensors $e_i\otimes1$ form a $K$-basis of $A$: the tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] give $a\otimes b=\sum_i(e_i\otimes1)\lambda_i(a)b$, so they span. For independence the bilinear maps $(a,b)\mapsto\lambda_i(a)b$ induce $K$-linear maps $A\to K$ taking $e_j\otimes1$ to $\delta_{ij}$; applying these to any relation makes every coefficient zero. Thus $\dim_K A=d>0$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. This uses a finite basis of $L/k$ only; $K/k$ can have arbitrary dimension.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 1.2.7, printed pp. 25--26; elementary scalar-extension basis calculation making the dimension input explicit

proof.text: For any prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, the quotient $A/\mathfrak p$ is a nonzero domain and is spanned over $K$ by the images of the $d$ basis vectors from Step 2. In particular it is finite-dimensional. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] to obtain that $A/\mathfrak p$ is a field. Step 1 therefore identifies it with $\kappa(z)$ over $K$, proving that every residue degree in the statement is finite.

source.place: Elementary finite-dimensional domain argument; compare Tag 00J6 (lemma-finite-dimensional-algebra) and the domain-is-field node

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian], the finite-dimensional commutative $K$-algebra $A$ is Artinian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-ideal-length-one-filtration] with $B=A$ and the unit ideal $J=A$. This gives $0=J_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq J_r=A$ with each $Q_i=J_i/J_{i-1}$ nonzero and having only the $A$-submodules $0$ and $Q_i$. Since $A\ne0$ by Step 2, $r>0$. These are also $K$-vector spaces with the induced scalar action.

source.place: Tags 00J6 (lemma-finite-dimensional-algebra), 00JB (lemma-artinian-finite-length), 00J3 (lemma-simple-pieces), applied to the unit ideal

proof.text: For each $i$, choose $0\ne q_i\in Q_i$. The image of $A\to Q_i$, $a\mapsto aq_i$, is a nonzero submodule, hence is all of $Q_i$. With $\mathfrak m_i=\{a:aq_i=0\}$, the formula $a\bmod\mathfrak m_i\mapsto aq_i$ is consequently a $K$-linear and $A$-linear bijection $A/\mathfrak m_i\simeq Q_i$. Every ideal strictly between $\mathfrak m_i$ and $A$ would give a nonzero proper submodule of this quotient, contradicting simplicity, so $\mathfrak m_i$ is maximal. Thus it is a prime ideal, and Step 3 and Step 1 identify $A/\mathfrak m_i$ with the residue field at a point $z_i\in P$. The scalar compatibility is built into the displayed formula: $(1\otimes c)aq_i=c(aq_i)$ for $c\in K$. Therefore $\dim_K Q_i=[\kappa(z_i):K]$.

source.place: Tag 00J2 (lemma-characterize-length-1), elementary cyclic-generator argument written out; no new lemma is used

proof.text: For every $i$, lift a $K$-basis of $Q_i$ to $J_i$ and adjoin a $K$-basis of $J_{i-1}$. The union spans $J_i$ because its images span the quotient, and is independent because reducing a relation modulo $J_{i-1}$ first kills the lifted coefficients and then the remaining coefficients. Hence $\dim_K J_i=\dim_K J_{i-1}+\dim_K Q_i$. (All these spaces are finite-dimensional subquotients of $A$.) Summing these equalities, and using Steps 2 and 5, yields $d=\sum_{i=1}^{r}[\kappa(z_i):K]$. If every summand were divisible by $\ell$, so would their sum $d$ be, contrary to the hypothesis. Choose a summand not divisible by $\ell$ and its point $z_i$. Together with Step 3 this proves both clauses. Repeated points in the list are allowed; they retain the multiplicities coming from nilpotents, so no reducedness or separability was assumed.

Source: ILO, Travaux de Gabber, Exposé II, Prop. 1.2.7 (printed pp. 25–26) says that for k'/k finite of degree prime to ℓ and any K/k, some residue field of k'⊗_k K has degree prime to ℓ over K. The item states exactly this, plus finiteness of every residue degree, which is true and is what the parent lem-per-alteration-cover-calculus uses in Steps 3 and 8 (with k=κ(x), L=κ(u), K=κ(y)). Small cases tested: L=k; C/R with K=C; Q(2^{1/3}) with K=R and with K=Q(2^{1/3}); the inseparable F_p(t^{1/p}) case, whose tensor algebra is nonreduced. Step 1 checked: it cites 01I4 (affine fibre product), 01JT (points), the residue-field sentence of 01JT (compatible with the map from K) and Spec of a field; each cited statement says what the step uses. Step 2 checked: the elementary basis argument gives dim_K A = d, with K-linearity checked and no finiteness of K/k used. Step 3 checked: A/p is a finite-dimensional domain, so the domain-is-field leaf applies with all its hypotheses, and Step 1 then gives κ(z) ≅ A/p over K. Step 4 checked: A is Artinian (00J6) and has a length-one filtration (00JB+00J3; that node allows non-local rings), with r>0. Step 5 checked: it writes out 00J2, Q_i ≅ A/m_i with m_i maximal, and the maximality argument is correct. Step 6 checked: dimension additivity gives d = Σ[κ(z_i):K] counted with multiplicity, and the divisibility contradiction follows. Tag labels 00J2/00J6/00JB/00J3/01I4/01JT checked against tags/tags. Route: the proof uses only definitions, Mathlib leaves and two nodes already proved in slopmaster2, which count as tools. The declared tool_use of lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field is accepted. The filtration degree sum covers both of ILO's cases (étale and radicial) at once; this is not a route departure.
